CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  June 10, 2019-2:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

D  SPECIAL MEETING

  Teleconference Location:
  Hyatt Regency Tamaya Resort and Spa
  1300 Tuyuna Trail, Santa Ana Pueblo, NM 87004
  Business Center

  OPENING:  Mayor Tornek called the special meeting to order at 4:01 p.m.
  ROLLCALL:  Mayor Terry Tornek
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Victor Gordo (Participated telephonically)
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Margaret McAustin (Absent)
  Councilmember Andy Wilson(Absent)

  Staff:  Steve Mermell, City Manager
  Julie Gutierrez, Assistant City Manager
  Michele Beal Bagneris, City Attorney/City Prosecutor
  Theresa Fuentes, Assistant City Attorney
  Matt Hawkesworth, Director of Finance
  Lori Eubanks, Senior Executive Assistant

  CITY MANAGER'S RECOMMENDED FISCAL YEAR 2020
  OPERATING BUDGET AND FISCAL YEAR.2020-2024 CAPITAL
  IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM (CIP) BUDGET:

  CIP and Operating Budget Presentations:
  • Water and Power
  Gurcharan Bawa, General Manager Water and Power, provided a
  PowerPoint presentation on the Department's Power and Water
  Fund Operating budgets, Electric and Water System CIP budgets,
  and Street Lighting and Electric Undergrounding Fund CIP budget;
  and responded to questions. Varoojan Avedian, Engineering
  Manager, responded to questions related to the replacement
  project of existing manhole covers/lids. Mitch Dion, Assistant
  General Manager Water and Power, responded to questions
  regarding the Department's preliminary non-potable water project,
  the impacts of the rainy season to ground water basin and surface
  water run-off levels, and active water wells in the City.

  City Manager Mermell responded to questions related to the City's
D  PMC, which does not allow for private water wells, and stated that
  staff will research the Annandale Golf Club's use of a private water
  well.

  Council Minutes  06/10/2019
   Councilmember Madison spoke on the need for staff to
  aggressively combat the affects of climate change through the
  City's policies and programs.

D  Councilmember Gordo requested that staff provide an update on
  the replacement project of the oil-based switches (in the vaults),
  including an anticipated completion date.

  Councilmember Hampton asked staff to follow up on the
  installation of a green mesh cover for the fencing surrounding the
  Sheldon Reservoir as part of the beautification efforts.

  Operating Budget Presentations:
  • Housing
  William Huang, Director of Housing, presented a PowerPoint
  presentation on the Housing Department's Operating budget, and
  responded to questions.

  The Mayor asked the Housing staff to provide additional
  clarification on the reallocation of funds that are included in the
  Housing Administration's Fiscal Year 2020 expenses.

  Councilmember Madison spoke on the need · for staff to work
  collaboratively with the United States Department of Veteran
  Affairs (VA) to investigate ways to better utilize the Veterans Affairs
  Supportive Housing (VASH) vouchers in the City. He also spoke
D  on the need to assist homeless students, specifically those
  attending Pasadena City College (PCC) to allow students to utilize
  their restroom facilities.

  Vice Mayor Hampton supported additional efforts to better utilize
  VASH vouchers, as well as ways to bridge the amount of available
  vouchers and the current rent market rate, to provide housing for
  homeless veterans. He also asked staff to consider ways to
  provide homeless individuals with access to basic hygiene
  facilities ; and provide information on the number of families that are
  provided assistance in the Pasadena Unified School District's
  Families In Transition program. Mr. Hampton also requested that
  staff consider partnering with other municipalities to build or
  convert housing opportunities for homeless individuals.

  The Mayor asked staff to clarify the number of affordable
  inclusionary units that were produced in Fiscal Year 2019.

  Councilmember Kennedy suggested that during the recruiting
  process of a MASH supervisor, staff do their best to find an
  individual who is empathetic to the needs of the community.

  Armando Herman, residence not stated, provided comment.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed .

  Council Minutes  2  06/10/2019
   ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the special meeting of the City Council
  adjourned at 5:46 p.m.
